title: HB310 (2021 Regular Session): Establishes the "Second Amendment Preservation Act," which creates additional protections to the right to bear arms

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk dataset (gun-policy Stage 5 LegiScan check); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official house.mo.gov or senate.mo.gov PDF of the version named in note (via LegiScan getBillText)

operative_text:
Section 1.420 (RSMo): (1) Any tax, levy, fee, or stamp imposed on firearms, firearm accessories, or ammunition not common to all other goods and services and that might reasonably be expected to create a chilling effect on the purchase or ownership of those items by law-abiding citizens;
Section 1.420 (RSMo): (4) Any act forbidding the possession, ownership, use, or transfer of a firearm, firearm accessory, or ammunition by law-abiding citizens; and
Section 1.420 (RSMo): (5) Any act ordering the confiscation of firearms, firearm accessories, or ammunition from law-abiding citizens.
Section 1.440 (RSMo): It shall be the duty of the courts and law enforcement agencies of this state to protect the rights of law-abiding citizens to keep and bear arms within the borders of this state and to protect these rights from the infringements defined under section 1.420.
Section 1.450 (RSMo): No entity or person, including any public officer or employee of this state or any political subdivision of this state, shall have the authority to enforce or attempt to enforce any federal acts, laws, executive orders, administrative orders, court orders, rules, regulations, statutes, or ordinances infringing on the right to keep and bear arms as described under section 1.410.
Section 1.460 (RSMo): 3. Sovereign, official, or qualified immunity shall not be an affirmative defense in such actions.
Section 1.470 (RSMo): 2. Neither the state nor any political subdivision of the state shall employ as a law enforcement officer or supervisor of law enforcement officers any person who is ineligible to serve in such capacity under this section.
